Aisha (CSM): Heads up — Crestline onboarding: we've been seeing 95th pct latency spikes during their batch ingest tests today. CPU OK, but p50 token latency jumps from ~40ms to ~220ms for some sequences.
Riley (Solutions): Oof, timeline? Is this only at higher seq lengths or across the board?
Aisha (CSM): Mostly at long-context sessions (>2k tokens) and when they switch to the richer summarization prompt. They ran a sustained test at ~120 qps and spikes correlated with cache misses.
Marco (Platform Eng): Do you have a sample trace or logs? Can you paste the /metrics/export snippet?
Aisha (CSM): Pasted below — there's a tiny trace.
Aisha (CSM): ```
request_id=crst-42 seq_len=2300 model=redwood-102b variant=fp16 latency_ms=218 p50_ms=42 p95_ms=218 kv_hit=false
request_id=crst-43 seq_len=512 model=redwood-102b variant=fp16 latency_ms=45 p50_ms=40 p95_ms=60 kv_hit=true
```
Jade (Support): Thanks — looks like KV cache miss pattern + heavy long-context tokens. For onboarding customers we usually nudge three things: (1) routing to dedicated pool for sustained qps, (2) int8 quantization profile on a compatible smaller variant to reduce kernel overhead, (3) enable prefix/KV warmup for known session IDs.
Riley (Solutions): Agree. Practical rollout: start with canary on their traffic to `redwood-63b-quant` (int8) and set routing rule to prefer dedicated nodes during 9a-5p PST tests only. If quality is acceptable we scale.
Marco (Platform Eng): From infra side, I can provision a small dedicated pool with reserved capacity and attach a routing policy: route-> if customer==crestline and qps>30 then dedicated-crestline. Also pre-populate KV cache for test sessions via a warmup job.
Aisha (CSM): Customer is nervous about model swaps hurting accuracy — they want a rollback plan.
Riley (Solutions): We'll run two A/B buckets: 5% traffic -> quantized 63B, 5% -> 13B-quant, rest baseline. Monitor rouge/semantic-similarity evals; auto-fallback to baseline if quality delta > 1.5% on eval set.
Jade (Support): I'll capture a 200-case prompt set from their prod-like corpus and run quick evals. Can you add these checkpoints to the rollout config?
Marco (Platform Eng): Yep. Add this snippet to the rollout policy (canary + auto-fallback):
```yaml
canary:
  - bucket: crestline-a  # 5%
    model: redwood-63b-quant
  - bucket: crestline-b  # 5%
    model: redwood-13b-quant
monitoring:
  eval_set: crestline-prompts-200
  quality_threshold: 0.985
  fallback: true
routing_rules:
  - condition: customer==crestline and qps>30
    target: dedicated-crestline
```
Aisha (CSM): Great. I'll sync with their PM and schedule the canary for tomorrow's 10:00 PST test window. Also asking them for the acceptance eval criteria.
Riley (Solutions): One more optimization: enable batching threshold reductions for long-context to prevent tails from forcing huge batches; set max_batch_tokens=4096 for dedicated-crestline.
Marco (Platform Eng): Noted. I'll put the config live and add a short runbook for rollback steps.
deploy-bot: deploy initiated for config dedicated-crestline at 1977655000 — status: queued. :gear:
Jade (Support): I'll run the evals and post results in this thread. Aisha, can you confirm stakeholder availability?
Aisha (CSM): Confirmed — PM + SRE are on board for 10am. I'll update after the canary. :thumbsup:
Riley (Solutions): Thanks team — nice proactive catch.
